 AG Uthmeier announces arrest of Kissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa
 BY 
 Kirstin Thomas , 
 Anthony Leone , 
 and 
 Spectrum News Staff
 Osceola County 
 UPDATED 10:21 AM ET Oct. 21, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 9:48 AM ET Oct. 21, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 9:48 AM EDT Oct. 21, 2026 
 SHARE 
 KISSIMMEE, Fla. — Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier posted on X Wednesday morning that Kissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa has been arrested and charged with grand theft and organized scheme to defraud.
 No other information has been released surrounding the charges.
 This morning, we arrested Kissimmee mayor Jackie Espinosa and are charging her with Grand Theft and Organized Scheme to Defraud. We will be holding a press conference at 2pm at our Orlando office with CFO Ingoglia and FDLE Commissioner Keefe to provide more information.
— Attorney General James Uthmeier (@AGJamesUthmeier) October 21, 2026 
 Uthmeier also noted on X that his office will hold a press conference at 2 p.m. from the Orlando office with Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia and Florida Department of Law Enforcement Commissioner Larry Keefe.
 Previous coverage 
 Florida CFO flags ‘troubling irregularities’ involving Kissimmee mayor, refers case to FDLE 
 Special prosecutor report says there is probable cause to pursue impeachment articles against Kissimmee mayor 
 Kissimmee mayor discusses report into grant involvement, awaits pending ethics review 
 Florida Commission on Ethics dismisses complaints against Kissimmee elected officials 
 Kissimmee commissioners will not move forward with impeachment of Mayor Jackie Espinosa 
 Espinosa, who took office in 2024, has been involved in some controversies. Over the summer, the Kissimmee City Commission decided not to move forward to impeach her from office . 
 Commissioners heard the findings of a special prosecutor's investigation that found probable cause to file articles of impeachment against Espinosa. However, during a special hearing in August, the city commissioners voted 2-2 on the question to whether or not advance the impeachment proceedings and go to trial. In order to move forward, a vote of 3-1 was required. 
 According to a report special prosecutor Mayanne Downs delivered in July , probable cause was found to pursue impeachment on three of seven alleged ethics violations involving $50,000 in city grant money awarded to three businesses owned by Espinosa or her family.
 The money came through the city’s Business Boost 2.0 program, which used American Rescue Plan Act funds to support businesses that suffered losses during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 The city’s written guidelines at the time did not prohibit elected officials from applying, but the 13-page report concluded that Espinosa's actions were serious enough to consider her removal from office.
 According to the report, the City Attorney’s Office “was not consulted on the application materials.”
 This is a developing story and more information will be provided as it becomes available.
